definitions.definition: A made-up field that combines theology (study of God) and physics (study of the universe) to explore how they might connect.
definitions.example: Like asking if the laws of physics could be related to spiritual ideas.

definitions.definition: A visual sketch or diagram used to explain complex ideas, like a chalkboard drawing in a classroom.
definitions.example: A teacher drawing a diagram of the solar system on a blackboard.

definitions.definition: A picture or diagram that helps explain something complicated.
definitions.example: A comic strip that shows how a car engine works.

definitions.definition: Designed to look sharp and clear on high-resolution screens, like those on modern phones and computers.
definitions.example: A photo that doesn't look blurry when you zoom in on a phone screen.

definitions.definition: A type of image file that keeps quality high and supports transparent backgrounds.
definitions.example: A logo saved as a PNG so it can be placed on different colored backgrounds without a white box around it.

definitions.definition: The main written work that explains the research or ideas in detail.
definitions.example: The textbook chapter that covers the main topic of a class.

definitions.definition: Facts, data, or examples that back up the main ideas or claims.
definitions.example: Witness statements and photos that prove someone was at a crime scene.

definitions.definition: The bigger picture or surrounding ideas that help you understand the main topic better.
definitions.example: Learning about the history of World War II to understand why a specific battle happened.
